newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Year-ahead inflation expectations fall - RBNZ survey.
newsitem.headline: Year-ahead inflation expectations fall - RBNZ survey.

text.p: Year-ahead inflation expectations have fallen slightly but GDP growth expectations are largely unchanged in a Reserve Bank of New Zealand survey published on Wednesday.

The bank said monetary conditions were perceived to have loosened since its August survey of expectations, with a net 63 percent of respondents now believing conditions to be tighter than usual. The corresponding figure for the August survey was 89 percent.

Respondents anticipate monetary conditions will have eased further by the end of March, with a net 32 percent of respondents expecting them to be tighter than neutral at that time. By September 1997, the corresponding figure is 22 percent.
The results represent the views of respondents in the financial, business, farming and labour branches of the economy, not those of the bank.
Respondents expect the Consumer Price Index to rise by 0.5 percent in the December 1996 quarter (unchanged from the previous survey) and by 0.4 percent in the March 1997 quarter.
For the year to September 1997, CPI inflation is expected to be 1.8 percent, down from 1.9 percent in the August survey.

Underlying inflation was expected to be 1.7 percent for the year to September 1997, versus 1.8 percent recorded in the previous survey, and to rise to 1.8 percent (versus 1.6 percent) in the year to September 1998.

Ninety-day bill rates are seen at 8.8 percent at the end of December 1996, slightly lower than at the time the survey was completed, and are expected to have fallen to 8.2 percent by the end of September 1997.

Ten-year government bond yields are expected to be 7.3 percent by the end of September 1997, from around 7.15 percent now. The Trade-Weighted Index was expected to be 66.7 at the end of March 1997 and 66.5 by end-September, from around 67.4 now.
Real GDP is expected to rise 2.4 percent in the year to September 1997, unchanged from the figure for the year to June recorded in the last survey.
A government surplus of NZ$2.5 billion is expected for the year to June 1997, compared with $2.8 billion in the August survey, and this is seen falling to $2.1 billion for the year to June 1998.
